title: "Hierarchical Clustering"
description: "A clustering method that builds a nested hierarchy of groups based on data similarity."
term: "Hierarchical Clustering"
letter: "H"
category: "Machine Learning"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

Hierarchical clustering organizes examples into nested groups. The
result can be displayed as a tree-like diagram, and a chosen cut through
that hierarchy gives a set of clusters.

## Technical explanation

Agglomerative methods start with individual examples and repeatedly
merge clusters according to a linkage criterion. Divisive methods begin
with one group and split it recursively. Linkage choices such as
single, complete, average, or Ward's method define how distances between
clusters are calculated.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

The hierarchy can help explore structure without choosing a cluster
count at the start. Results can be sensitive to distance, scaling,
linkage, and outliers, and many implementations have substantial
memory or runtime costs for large datasets.

## How it works

Calculate pairwise distances or another similarity measure. Repeatedly
merge the closest clusters under the chosen linkage, recording the
merge distance. A dendrogram or related representation shows the
sequence of merges; selecting a cut determines the final grouping.

## Practical example

A team can cluster document embeddings hierarchically and inspect a
dendrogram to explore broad themes and their subtopics.

## Common misconceptions

- The hierarchy is not automatically a meaningful taxonomy.
- The number of clusters still must be selected when a flat assignment
  is needed.
- Different distance and linkage choices can produce different trees.
